plan_a_advantages: Includes a tempo run to develop threshold speed, a key component of faster running.
Features a longer run to build endurance and trail-specific durability.
Provides a more balanced approach to training, incorporating both easy and hard efforts.
plan_b_advantages: May be suitable for an athlete who is currently overtrained or injured and needs a very low-impact week.
The focus on easy running could be beneficial for building a base level of aerobic fitness if the athlete is very new to trail running.
reasoning: Plan A is the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. While both plans prioritize easy running, Plan A incorporates a tempo run and a longer run, which are crucial for developing speed and endurance respectively. Plan B focuses almost exclusively on easy runs and rest, which is appropriate for recovery but insufficient for actively improving performance. The inclusion of structured intensity work in Plan A makes it more effective for achieving the stated goal.
